subject: cherryBlossom
pitch:
Category: Plant.
Subject: cherry blossom tree.
Style: ukiyo-e woodblock print.
reasoning:
I'm planning out a cherry blossom tree model as a static plant, deciding to skip joints and rig setup since it doesn't need articulation, and considering using swept paths for the trunk shape.

For the design I'm sketching a leaning gnarled trunk with sweeping branches, blossom clusters built from flat-shaded icosahedron blobs, and a ukiyo-e palette of sumi ink, bark browns, soft pinks, and touches of Prussian blue, keeping the composition focused on the tree itself without ground elements or extra props. Now I'm working out the texture list for the piece.

I'm planning out decal textures: a five-petal blossom cluster card with ink outlines and pink gradient, a single petal card for loose falling petals, a small red-brown young leaf card, a red hanko seal decal with an abstract "桜"-like glyph for the trunk, and a hanging tanzaku poem strip with a cord and vertical calligraphy-style strokes as a modest ukiyo-e accent.

Now I'm settling on seven total texture elements — blossom cluster, single flower, petal, bud sprig, leaf, tanzaku, seal — plus bark, blossom mass, and root paint layers, and sketching the trunk's leaning S-curve path with tapering radii from base to crown.

For the trunk cross-section I'm going faceted rather than smooth, using an eight-sided circle with smooth shading disabled for that woodblock-print look. Then I'm working out root flares as swept sprouts radiating from the base, tapering and sinking slightly below the ground plane so they read as rooted into the floor.

I'm adjusting the trunk's cap settings so the start sits flat right at floor level instead of a rounded cap that would dip below it, while the end keeps a round cap. Then I'm sketching a reusable branch helper that sweeps points and radii, returning the path so child branches and blossoms can attach at specific points along it, with children starting from plain offset points rather than full skeletons.

Now I'm working through burying child branch roots inside their parent's tube by starting them at a centerline point from the parent path, hiding the flat start cap when the child radius is smaller. I'm sketching a recursive growth function that builds curved branch paths with a seed-based random generator, recursing into child branches at points along the curve and collecting twig endpoints for later blossom placement.

Rather than fully proceduralizing the composition, I think hand-placing five dramatic main limbs with an asymmetric sweep -- echoing Hiroshige-style overhanging branches -- then layering procedural sub-branches on top will read more convincingly. I'm budgeting the geometry: roughly 120 branch sweeps at ~72 triangles each, around 5k triangles of icosahedron blossom blobs across 60 clusters, and up to 400 lightweight four-triangle blossom cards merged by texture to stay well within the triangle and part limits.

For the canopy, I'm picturing blossom puffs as flat-shaded, irregularly scaled icosahedra painted with a mottled pink-to-pale two-tone cel shade, lighter on top. I'd scatter flower-cluster cards across the merged puff surfaces using a surface scatter with minimum distance to avoid overlap, which should stay cheap computationally even with hundreds of candidate points. I'm also weighing whether to pull in a toon kit for the cel shading, since a hard two-tone flat color with a soft bokashi-style gradient feels right for the ukiyo-e aesthetic.

Since outlining the blobs with a true ink rim isn't straightforward without a back-face trick, I'm leaning toward faking it with a keyline-style paint that divides the blossom surface into irregular cells separated by thin deep-pink lines, mimicking the clustered, faintly outlined look of traditional cherry blossom prints.

Everything I need (noise, cells, mix, smoothstep, paint) comes from the single SDK entry point, so no extra kits are necessary — I'll skip lanterns or glow effects to keep complexity down. For the trunk, I'm planning a sumi-ink bark paint: a cool dark grey-brown base with lighter blue-grey patches and horizontal lenticel dashes, since that horizontal banding is a distinctive, recognizable feature of real cherry bark.

Writing bark texture noise...

I also want moss accents on upward-facing surfaces near the base, using normal direction and noise to blend a green-grey tint in low areas of the trunk.

For falling petals, I'm placing around 40 small flat quad cards scattered near the lower portion of the tree, each with random position, direction, and orientation to mimic ukiyo-e-style falling blossoms drifting through the air and settling near the ground.

Now I'm designing the flower sprig texture in SVG, drawing clusters of five-petal sakura flowers with heart-notched petal tips using a defined petal path.

Writing flower cluster code...

At lean 90 the card face normal points straight up along the facing axis, lying flat against the surface, so I'll randomize the flow direction per card to get varied tilt rather than a uniform back-facing lean, settling on lean around 80 for a near-flat decal look.

I'm adding a slight lift so puffs don't z-fight with the surface, then thinking about scattering small bronze-red and light green leaf cards near the puff edges to mimic young Yamazakura leaves emerging alongside the blossoms, and shaping the puff geometry as a flattened icosahedron.

Now I'm planning around 55 puffs of varying radius to build dense, layered canopy clouds typical of Japanese tree styling, with shared paint patterns across puffs. I'm starting to lay out the branch structure, with the trunk rising and splitting into limbs sweeping outward on each side.

Defining limb geometry...

Working out branch placement for child limbs...

Still refining branch curve points...

I'm planning the branching hierarchy—5 main limbs each with 4 depth-1 kids, each with 3 twigs, totaling around 85 segments plus trunk and roots, staying under 200. For leaf puffs, I'll place them at branch and twig tips, then thin the roughly 80 candidates by rejecting any within 0.6 distance of an already-accepted puff, leaving around 50 well-spaced clusters.

Now I'm positioning each puff slightly above its tip with randomized radius and a flattened vertical scale, checking none dip below ground level, plus adding a central top puff for fullness. For the weeping sakura effect I'm adding hanging blossom-strand cards beneath puffs, oriented upward with a 180-degree lean so they drape downward like tassels in a ukiyo-e style.

Cards should use cross:true so they're visible from the front but edge-on from the sides, since the card plane sits in the facing/width directions. I'm also thinking about fallen petals as flat cards on the ground, and about hanging a tanzaku strip from a branch point with a thin cord dropping down before the paper plane begins.

For the paper strip itself, I'm picturing a textured 0.07×0.35 panel, cream-white with calligraphy and a reddish gradient band at the top. Since a single plane only shows its texture from one side, I'm considering using two back-to-back planes facing opposite directions so the drawing reads correctly from both sides without mirroring issues.

I'm also thinking about adding a red hanko seal decal near the lower front of the trunk as a nice ukiyo-e-style signature touch, placing it at a point on the trunk sweep facing forward.

Actually, a seal directly on the tree feels gimmicky — maybe better placed on the tanzaku instead. A more fitting idea is to give the old cherry tree a sacred shimenawa rope with zigzag shide paper, which is a classic and iconic detail for venerable shrine trees.

I'll drop the tanzaku and seal to keep things simple, settling on shimenawa with shide as the single accessory. Now I'm working out the geometry — looping the straw rope around the trunk's centerline using the path's position at a given parameter rather than the surface point.

For the twisted rope texture, I'm figuring out the diagonal stripe pattern by computing the number of twists needed given the rope's circumference and desired twist spacing (roughly 23 turns over 2.8m), then setting up a modulo condition on the angle-around-tube and position-along-tube to create spiraling stripes.

For the sweep itself, I'll close the loop path and skin it into a tube of radius 0.045, maybe giving it a slight sag to look like a hanging rope.

Then for the shide, I'm planning to add zigzag white paper streamers hanging from the rope, plus a pendant tassel element.

For positioning the shide cards, I'll sample points along the rope's parametric path, placing each card frame oriented outward with a lean, concentrated around the front arc where t=0 corresponds to the +Z direction and increasing t sweeps toward +X.

So the root edge should be drawn at the SVG bottom, since that corresponds to the top edge in world space where the shide attaches to the rope; the zigzag then narrows there and widens toward the SVG top.

I'm considering extra trunk details too: a dark knothole decal on the lower trunk, scattered lichen patches, and maybe small burl spheres stuck on the bark via surface scatter with bark-matching paint.

For the base, I'm sketching flared roots radiating from the trunk base using swept curves—six roots going from inside the trunk down to the ground, tapering in radius as they spread outward.

I'm working out the trunk points with lean, S-curve, and slight twist, with limbs branching off the trunk path at specific parameters using radii smaller than the trunk's at that point so junctions blend naturally. Trunk radii taper from 0.52 down to 0.2 at the rounded top, with limb radii around 0.16-0.2 near their junctions.

I'm now defining actual coordinates: five trunk path points with slight x/z offsets for the curve, plus a matching radii array. For the limbs, I'm plotting out branch A starting around t=0.86 on the trunk, curving outward and upward to a tip near (2.9, 3.3, 0.3) with tapering radius, and starting to sketch branch B on the opposite side.

Still plotting branch coordinates...

With all seven limbs placed, I'm checking the overall bounding box: roughly -2.3 to 2.9 on x, and a total height near 5.7 meters including the foliage puffs on top.

I'm designing a recursive branching function that spawns child limbs from each parent path point, with decreasing counts at each depth—5 kids at the mid-branch level, 3 at the next, tapering down to twig tips. That gives roughly 147 branch sweeps total, and estimating triangle counts across branches, foliage puffs, and flower cards lands around 25k triangles, which seems reasonable, though I might trim the twig count at the deepest level to save some budget.

Child length and radius scale down from the parent using lerp ratios, and I'm adding slight random jitter via catmull points to get that angular, ukiyo-e twiggy look rather than smooth curves. Blossom and foliage anchors sit at the branch tips across all three depths, and I'm scattering small bronze-green leaf cards near the puffs for added texture, drawing them directly in color rather than using a texture map.

Now I'm checking paint texel density across the whole tree -- with puffs covering roughly 165 m² of surface, a 1024 sheet gives too coarse a resolution (~1.6cm/texel), so bumping to a 2048 paint sheet improves bark and lenticel detail while staying under the atlas limit. For thin twigs, I'll skip painting entirely and just use a flat dark brownish-purple color to save texture budget.

Now I'm sketching the ukiyo-e palette: a near-black sumi ink, a few bark tones for bokashi gradients, moss green, a run of cherry-blossom pinks from pale to deep with a line-ink pink-red, bronze for branches, leaf green, and straw tones for highlights.

For the blossom paint function, I'm using Worley cell noise to carve petal shapes, drawing a keyline where cell edges are thin, and blending pink tones top-to-bottom (bokashi-style) with a deeper shadow mix on the underside where the normal points downward.

Now I'm moving on to the bark paint function, layering dark and mid brown tones through noise, adding cooler highlights on upward-facing surfaces, then stretching noise along a vertical axis to carve horizontal lenticel marks into the bark texture.

Still working through branch texturing...

Now I'm scattering burl growths onto the trunk surface, filtering by height range to keep them in a believable band.

Placing a knot decal near the trunk front, computing its surface position along the trunk path.

No collision at that height, so that's fine. For the trunk I'll keep smooth off with 8 sides for a faceted low-poly look, and plan flowers to go on the puffs after they're placed rather than directly on twigs. Now I'm building the SVG string for the flower cluster texture.

Writing flower petal SVG...

I'm setting the gradient direction vertically so the petal base is deep-colored and the tip fades pale, and checking the outline stroke width scales sensibly at the target viewBox size before working out overall flower proportions.

I'm placing four flowers at varied positions, scales, and rotations within the cluster, verifying their bounding boxes stay inside the canvas, and adding a few small bud ellipses to fill gaps. The stylized flower size runs larger than a real cherry blossom, which is fine for this design, and I'm confirming the background stays transparent for proper cutout compositing before starting a separate single-petal texture at a smaller viewBox.

Now I'm designing a single pointed petal with a notch and pink gradient, scaling and positioning it to fit a 32x32 canvas, then planning ground-lying fallen petals and a hanging flower strand with a wavy stem and blossoms spaced along its length.

I'm reconsidering the strand's scale and stroke widths so flowers stay visible at small sizes, deciding to bump the canvas resolution and make stroke width a function of each flower's scale so outlines stay crisp.

Now I'm sketching the leaf texture as a bronze-to-green gradient leaf shape with a dark outline and center vein, rooted at the bottom of its viewBox so it attaches naturally, then moving on to design the shide paper streamer as a zigzag folded strip anchored at the bottom too.

Writing shide polygon points...

Now I'm sketching the knot texture as a small gradient ellipse with a dark outer ring and lighter inner ring, giving it a bark-like decal appearance. That brings the texture set to six: cluster, petal, strand, leaf, shide, and knot, which feels sufficient for the design.

I'm working out where strands and flower cards should scatter across the puffs, filtering by surface normal so hanging strands appear on undersides and flowers populate the upper puff surfaces, aiming for roughly 260 flower cards across the puff surface area.

I'll settle on around 480 flower cards sized 0.26 with a single scatter pass and minDist 0.12, keeping puff count near 45 so they're bigger and fewer to cut overhead. For ground clutter, I'll scatter 90 fallen petals lying flat in a ring plus 40 petals drifting in the air at random positions and leans without sinking.

Now I'm setting up the actual build function: importing the builder utilities, defining the module-level palette and petal textures, then starting the trunk's spline path with control points sweeping from the base up through the canopy.

I'm tuning the trunk's radius taper so the base flares out wider with a gnarly root-like bulge before narrowing toward the top.

Now I'm generating seven root sweeps radiating outward from the trunk base at jittered angles, using curved paths that start thick near the trunk and taper thin as they extend outward along the ground.

Then I'm writing a recursive growth function for limbs: each branch sweeps a tapered tube, colored bark for thicker branches and twig color for the finest, then spawns child branches at points along its length with slightly randomized positions, continuing to a set depth before collecting tip points for leaves or fruit placement later.

Adding a minimum length clamp and extra downward droop for weeping-branch twigs, then laying out the branch's curve points with some wobble offset between base and end.

I'm tapering the radii per segment and recursing into the next depth level for child growth. Checking that depth-1 droop doesn't push tips below the ground bound, then tallying up the total branch/twig counts across all seven limbs to sanity-check the structure.

Now I'm generating puff clusters at branch tips, spacing them apart with a minimum distance check and randomizing their size and squashed scale to look like foliage clumps.

Still writing puff placement logic...

Scattering flower clusters across the canopy surface using sampled hit points with minimum distance spacing, filtering by normal direction to avoid downward-facing puffs, then placing blossom cards at those positions.

Still defining leaf and strand placement...

Repeated calls to scatter on the same surface give different point placements, which is fine. I'm placing a shimenawa girth loop around the trunk at a specific point along its path, using a direction and lift offset to position it correctly.

Since the trunk is a faceted octagon, the rope sweep's thickness and lift need to cover that geometry, which they do. I'm considering shide paper streamers hanging at specific intervals along the rope, computing their positions and orientation frames along the girth path.

Each shide should flow outward radially from the trunk's horizontal center, so I'm computing the direction vector from the trunk's approximate centerline. I'm also setting up a scatter of burl bumps across the trunk surface, filtering by height and normal direction so they avoid the rope band and don't appear on downward-facing areas.

For the knot decal, I'm casting a ray from outside the trunk toward its center to find the exact surface hit point, then placing the decal there with a guard in case the ray misses.

Now I'm checking paint callback signatures, making sure unused parameters are underscored properly and that the return type matches the expected Rgb format.

For the blossom coloring, I'm working through a woodblock-style quantization: blending pink tones based on lift and cell id, then thinking about snapping the blend into discrete tonal bands via thresholds rather than smooth gradients to get that hard-edged print look.

Still refining petal highlight logic...

Now setting twig color, rope paint selection with noise flecks, and starting to write the SVG path strings and defs for petals...

Writing SVG path definitions...

Still writing flower center details...

Checking petal sizing fits within bounds, then designing the strand layout: a curved stem path with flowers positioned bottom-to-top at varying scales and rotations, plus a bud at the top.

I'm sketching the remaining decal pieces—leaf and shide dimensions, and a knot shape built from layered ellipses with a cutout highlight for the braided texture. I'm also confirming the decal and texture call signatures before writing out the full component code.

Scattering fallen petals around the base, randomizing their angle and radius so they cluster near the trunk and thin out further away, with some variation in size and orientation for a natural look.

I'm setting the airborne petal positions to float above and in front of the tree, keeping them within a reasonable range so they don't collide with the foliage clusters, and double-checking that the trunk's circular cross-section options, card frame signatures, and hanging strand flow functions all match the API's expected shapes.

Verifying scatter option names and the random generator's calling convention before finalizing variable typing to keep things clean for strict TypeScript. Now writing the final tree-generation code with trunk root radius adjustments.

Checking each limb's start radius against the trunk's taper at its attachment point to make sure branches emerge naturally without clipping into or floating off the trunk surface.
